next_steps.action: Disconnect adapter and battery. CPU VRM rails have a very low normal resistance to ground (single-digit ohms is common due to the many output capacitors). Compare against a known-good board.

measure.where: CPU socket VCORE pins or the VRM inductor output pads
measure.expected: Highly board-dependent — typically 5-30 ohm. Compare to known-good. Values below 2 ohm with no load on the rail suggest a shorted output FET or output cap.
measure.safety: VRM rails hold charge in many ceramics — wait for full discharge before measuring.

interpretations.if_result: Resistance much lower than known-good board
interpretations.then: Short on VCORE. Suspect low-side MOSFET(s) or output cap. Do NOT apply power; hunt the short first.
No short. Proceed to check VRM input supply.

next_steps.requires_info_note: A known-good board reading is strongly recommended — CPU VRM resistance is too board-specific to interpret alone.
